page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2688.78. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 10787.62 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5770.0. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 25%, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression is also weak. However, cache-bound operations perform adequately, with small-block read memory bandwidth reaching 508.47 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-8 offers a dense allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources at a lower price tier compared to memory-rich instances. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained memory capacity of 8.0 GB for an 8-vCPU configuration, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications.

This server configuration is best suited for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints, such as web serving, lightweight software compilation, and basic text or image processing tasks.
